evals.name: A method and no source material
evals.prompt: I'm a behavioral scientist at Irrational Labs. I want to turn the 'saying-is-believing' technique from Walton & Cohen's belonging work into a skill for the besci-skills library. Users would be NGO program staff designing a storytelling intervention. Can you help me build it? I'm in Claude Code.
evals.expected_output: The interview starts and nothing is drafted: one question on the first gate (what the skill does in one sentence), with a recommended answer, and the gates it can check itself (common, distinct) reported as looked up rather than asked.
assertions: Asks exactly one question and stops.
The question is about a gate and carries a recommended answer.
The question is about the method, not about sections of the spec.
Does not ask the author which sources name the task or whether a similar skill exists; it looks these up or says it will.
Does not write SKILL.md or any other file yet.

evals.name: A workflow presented as a skill
evals.prompt: Make me a skill that designs a complete behavior change program for an NGO, from understanding the problem to designing the intervention and planning the evaluation.
evals.expected_output: The first gate fails: this is several skills. The creator proposes the split, notes that most of the pieces already exist in the library, and asks which one to build now. It does not draft one large skill.
assertions: Says the request is more than one skill.
Proposes a split into named pieces.
Asks which piece to build now, or points to the existing skills or a workflow that cover it.
Does not draft a skill that covers the whole program.

evals.name: A revision after a review
evals.prompt: The reviewer said the trigger rule on my skill draft-norms-vignette is too vague and it fires on requests that belong to write-social-norm-message. Can you fix it? The repo is open here.
evals.expected_output: The creator reads the skill's folder, changelog, and any open expert review first, then asks one question, with a recommended answer, about what should change before it edits anything.
assertions: Reads, or says it will read, the skill folder and its changelog before proposing a change.
Asks one question about the intended change before editing a file.
Does not rewrite parts of the skill the request did not mention.
Mentions that the version and the changelog change together, or that the changelog entry cites the review.

evals.name: Not for this library
evals.prompt: I want to create a skill that formats Excel spreadsheets with our company's brand colors.
evals.expected_output: The creator says this is not a behavioral-science library skill and points to Anthropic's general skill-creator, without starting the interview.
assertions: Says the skill does not belong in this library.
Points to Anthropic's general skill-creator.
Does not start the interview.

evals.name: A source to read first
evals.prompt: Here's a chapter from our field playbook on running a barrier analysis with doers and non-doers. Turn it into a library skill. [chapter text follows: purpose, the doer/non-doer survey, sample of 45 and 45, the six standard determinant questions, tabulation, and the rule for calling a difference meaningful]
evals.expected_output: The creator works from the source and asks only what it does not answer, such as where the method goes wrong in practice or what a good result looks like, and checks the early gates, including whether an existing skill already produces this output.
assertions: Does not ask the author to restate what the chapter already says.
Asks one question at a time, and only about what the source does not cover.
Raises at least one early gate: one thing, common, adds something, or distinct from existing skills.
Does not write the whole folder in the first reply.
